figures.title: The completed rectangular transpose
figures.caption: The ordinary transpose returns fifteen elements before the caller stores the count.
figures.alt: Five annotated details from the same ordinary transpose boundary. Rows is three, columns five and the returned count fifteen. Output contains five rows of three words. The 128-byte fully associative cache records thirty accesses, twenty-two hits and eight misses, or a rounded seventy-three percent hit rate.

figures.title: Finish one clipped tile
figures.caption: The first clipped tile is complete; the second tile has not begun.
figures.alt: Five annotated details at the second next tile boundary. The input is three by five. Tile origin registers are row zero and column four. The fully associative 128-byte cache records twenty-four accesses and seven misses, with a rounded seventy-one percent hit rate.

figures.title: A fully associative tiled measurement
figures.caption: The completed sixteen-by-sixteen tiled transpose records 128 fully associative misses.
figures.alt: Five annotated details after the sixteen-by-sixteen tiled routine returns. Both dimensions are hexadecimal ten, or decimal sixteen; the returned count is hexadecimal one hundred, or decimal two hundred fifty-six. The first output row is shown. Eight fully associative four-word blocks record 512 accesses, 384 hits and 128 misses, for a seventy-five percent hit rate.

figures.title: The same tile with direct mapping
figures.caption: Direct mapping gives 344 misses for the same completed tiled transpose and cache capacity.
figures.alt: Five annotated details from a separate direct-mapped execution of the same sixteen-by-sixteen tiled routine. Dimensions, returned count and output match the fully associative run.
